title: Evidence requirements for compassionate release of super applications

sections.heading: Providing required evidence
sections.text:
Each category of compassionate release of super has specific evidence you must provide to support the eligibility of the:

- claim
- expense amount.

You will need to provide additional evidence if you:

- are requesting to pay expenses for another person and you have either an interdependency relationship or a substantial financial dependency relationship with them
- borrowed money to pay for the expense and you are unable to pay the outstanding amount.

If you don't provide all required evidence your application will be delayed or will not be approved.

sections.heading: Format of evidence documents
sections.text: Understand the following requirements which apply to the evidence and information that you provide:

sections.heading: Format of evidence documents > Statutory declarations
sections.text: You can make a Commonwealth statutory declaration via the paper form or through your myGov account. You can also use any state or territory statutory declaration form, so long as it meets the requirements of the Act it is made under.

sections.heading: Format of evidence documents > Online applications
sections.text:
If you submit your application online, you need to provide digital copies of the required evidence. Please note:

- We do accept photos of documents. The supported file formats are PDF, gif, jpeg and png.
- We do **not** accept screen shots of text messages or emails.
- Our system will not accept more than 20 attachments. The maximum size for an attachment is 10 MB.

sections.heading: Format of evidence documents > Paper applications
sections.text: If you submit a paper application, you need to ensure you provide copies of your documents. **Do not provide the original documents** as these will not be returned.

sections.heading: Format of evidence documents > Evidence in a language other than English
sections.text:
If your evidence, including quotes and invoices or registered medical practitioner and specialist reports, are written in a language other than English you will need to have it translated.

The translator must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters (NAATI).

sections.heading: Format of evidence documents > Images
sections.text: Do **not** include images of a disturbing nature to support your application, as they're not necessary to assess your application.

sections.heading: Format of evidence documents > Financial statements
sections.text:
When providing financial statements (for example, from a lender) to support your application, you need to:

- ensure these are on the provider's letterhead
- include the account holder’s name and the statement period.

sections.heading: Relevant registered medical specialists
sections.text:
Application for medical treatment or transport require at least one medical report to be provided by a specialist in the area that you're applying to have medical treatment for. If you’re applying for:

- treatment of life-threatening illness or injury, one medical report must be from a registered medical specialist whose speciality is relevant to the life-threatening illness or injury. For example, if you're applying to pay for an expense to treat cancer, the specialist will be an oncologist
- treatment of an acute or chronic mental illness, your application must include a medical report from a psychiatrist (not a psychologist)
- dental treatment to alleviate acute or chronic pain, you can provide either

- one report from a registered medical practitioner and one report from a dental practitioner
- a medical report from 2 separate dental practitioners
- dental treatment to alleviate acute or chronic mental illness, your application must include

- a medical report from a dental practitioner
- a medical report from a psychiatrist (not a psychologist).

Allied professionals, such as physiotherapists, psychologists and podiatrists, are **not** considered registered medical practitioners or medical specialists.

sections.heading: Quotes or unpaid invoices
sections.text:
Invoices and quotes must:

- be on the provider's letterhead
- be addressed to you, or your dependant if you are applying for them
- include the provider's name and contact details
- include an **itemised list** of expenses and their respective costs. Lump sum quotes or invoices won't be accepted
- be converted to Australian dollars if they're in a foreign currency. The conversion must be at the exchange rate at the time you apply. If we approve your application, we won't recalculate the conversion at the time of approval.

sections.heading: Quotes or unpaid invoices > Paid invoices
sections.text:
If the expense you are applying for was paid by borrowing money, your paid invoice, receipt or bank statement that shows the payment of the expense, will need to include the:

- date of payment
- method of payment (electronic payment, credit card, cash)
- amount paid
- payer's details.

Where you are providing bank statements, you need to ensure that the account holder's name and statement period are visible.

sections.heading: Timing of requirements
sections.text:
When providing documents to support your application, you need to ensure they meet the timing requirements. These requirements apply from the date your application is submitted and differ depending on the type of document being provided, as follows:

- Medical reports must be completed, signed and dated less than 6 months old.
- Quotes must be dated less than 6 months old.
- Invoices must be dated less than 30 days old.
- Utility bills must be less than 3 months old.
- Letters indicating foreclosure action must be less than 30 days old.

sections.heading: Paid by borrowing money
sections.text:
If the expense you are applying for was paid by borrowing money, there are no time requirements for documents, unless they relate to preventing foreclosure or forced sale of your home.

If your application related to preventing foreclosure or forced sale of your home, you will need to provide:

- documents from your lender showing the value of 3 months repayments and 12 months interest at the time the amount was owing. Documents that can be provided include mortgage statements for the period or a letter from your lender
- default notice or equivalent notice from your mortgagee that relates to the amount that was owing
- utility bill (such as for gas or electricity) dated within 3 months of the above documents, in your name and that shows the address of the property.

sections.heading: Validation checks
sections.text:
We may carry out checks with your providers to validate evidence provided in your application. This may include contacting service providers to:

- validate invoices, quotes or medical reports
- ask for missing or additional information that is required.
